acceptanceClaims: delivered and undelivered histories physically produced different evaluator ground truth but byte-identical durable sender ledgers and byte-identical post-crash successor views
both byte-identical successor views classified UNKNOWN and authorized neither blind resend nor completion publication
a restricted UID-65534 blind resend duplicated the delivered history to two total pulses while applying the undelivered history exactly once
recipient-side durable effect identity remained unreadable to the restricted successor while the same principal retained capability to resend the public exact effectId
with recipient duplicate suppression, delivered-history retry returned duplicate-suppressed and undelivered-history retry returned applied, while both recipient states converged to applicationCount=1
both idempotent-retry histories returned acknowledgement sufficient for sender completion and the public Unix-domain capability endpoint closed with zero residuals
limitations: the accepted result is limited to one owned local no-uplink Unix-domain consequence and one recipient-private durable dedup store
the evaluator-only oracle establishes experimental ground truth but is intentionally outside successor authority and is not a recovery mechanism
atomicity between an irreversible downstream consequence and recipient dedup persistence is not proved
recipient-state loss, corruption, partitions, multiple recipients, shared resources and generic exactly-once semantics remain unproved
no external or uncontrolled target authority is admitted
